5.0.0.en: This is an example of a trial that afflicts the Church from within, unlike the persecutions by the leaders of the Jews that afflicted it from outside.

5.0.1.en: Behold Ananias, whose name means "the Lord's grace," and Sapphira his wife, whose name means "shining," sell a field for the need of the Church, as many were doing.

5.1.0.en: But they wanted to hide part of the price and keep it for themselves while claiming that what they would give to the Apostles was the whole price. They agreed on this and carried it out out of love of appearing generous and giving lavishly, though it was their right to keep one part and give the other. But it was the sin of hypocrisy and love of show that led to the lie, and by their lie they are counted as thieves of part of God's money, which they claimed to have given to Him, namely the whole price of the field.

5.2.0.en: Peter declared to Ananias the gravity of his yielding to Satan, who had filled his heart with love of show, and this means that Ananias could have driven out the evil thoughts of Satan but was negligent because of his pride. This perhaps also shows the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, for He is one of the hypostases of the Trinity and not merely the power of God, as claimed by the heretic Macedonius, whom the Church calls the enemy of the Holy Spirit and who was anathematized by the Council of Constantinople.

5.3.0.en: Conceived this thing in your heart: that is, he intended evil or planned the intention for it.

5.3.1.en: Peter explained to Ananias that he had the right to dispose of his property as he wished, so he need not sell the field if he did not want to, and likewise he could give all its price or part of it. The Apostle rebuked him for his lie because it was directed to God before men.

5.3.2.en: Know that every sin we commit against a person is directed first toward God, as David the prophet said, "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned" (Ps 51:4). So do not forget the presence of God, but for His sake keep away from sin so as not to anger Him, and remind yourself that He stands before you and sees all your deeds, words and thoughts, and even if you fall, hasten to repent to Him and He will forgive you and you will escape all punishment.

5.4.0.en: God's punishment was immediate, with the death of Ananias as he fell, which put the fear of God in the hearts of the believers. This was necessary at the beginning of the Church so that they would reject sin and be careful about their lives, and it also gave awe to the Apostles, for they had the gift of revealing the unseen, so the Holy Spirit gave Peter to know what Ananias and his wife Sapphira had done.

5.4.1.en: If you suffer from laziness and negligence, remember the judgment of God so that you fear Him and keep away from sin, for love alone is not enough for your salvation, but also the fear of God and the rejection of the sin that causes your destruction. This is why the Church reminds you every day before you sleep, in the prayer of sleep in the Agpeya, that you will stand before the just Judge, so that you feel terrified and trembling because of your many sins, and it leads you to repentance and the salvation of your soul and you enjoy the sweetness of fellowship with Him and His overflowing love.

5.5.0.en: The young men buried Ananias outside the city of Jerusalem, in which the Jews did not allow anyone to be buried.

5.6.0.en: The gathering of the believers continued for three hours, during which Ananias was buried, and after that his wife Sapphira came, not knowing what had happened to her husband, but thinking that the deceit and lie they had agreed on had succeeded.

5.7.0.en: The price of the field was still laid before the Apostles when Sapphira came in, so Peter hastened to ask her whether this sum was the whole price of the field, to give her an opportunity to repent and declare the truth, but unfortunately she persisted in the lie she had agreed on with her husband.

5.7.1.en: Do not indulge others in breaking God's commandments, lying so that they will not be angry with you, or agreeing to any sin and sharing in it, such as condemnation or foul words... You are responsible for every word that comes out of your mouth.

5.7.2.en: May you take care to please God before pleasing men.

5.8.0.en: To tempt the Spirit of the Lord: by Ananias and Sapphira doubting the ability of the Apostles to uncover the truth of their deceit through the Holy Spirit.

5.8.1.en: The feet of them which have buried your husband: that is, the young men were about to arrive at the place of the gathering after burying Ananias.

5.8.2.en: The Apostle Peter declares the agreement of the couple in evil and consequently the necessity of punishment falling on them.

5.9.0.en: Sapphira fell down dead, and the young men who had buried her husband arrived and carried her out to bury her.

5.10.0.en: All feared God, whether they were members of the Church or the rest of the Jews in Jerusalem.

5.10.1.en: Here in the Book of Acts the word "church" is used for the first time.

5.11.0.en: Miracles took place at the hands of the Apostles confirming the truth of their message openly before all the people. And all of them, in unity of the Spirit, prayed in Solomon's Porch.

5.12.0.en: As for those outside the faith, they feared the believers and the Apostles and held them in honor because of their purity and the power of God working in them.

5.13.0.en: New believers continued to join, and their number was not mentioned as it was the last time, when he said five thousand, because the number had greatly increased. He made clear here what he had not made clear before, that they were men and women, to show the importance of woman, like man, in the Church.

5.14.0.en: Beds: soft, furnished couches suitable for the rich.

5.14.1.en: Couches: rough, and used by the poor.

5.14.2.en: The sick, rich (carrying them on beds) and poor (laying them on couches), were healed by the mere falling of the shadow of the Apostle Peter on them, without his even touching them. For God wanted to show the power of His Holy Spirit in His Apostles, in that their shadow alone was enough to heal diseases, especially since the number crowded around them seeking healing was very great.

5.15.0.en: The healing of the sick was not limited to the residents of Jerusalem, but included also those coming from the cities around it. And it was not only healing of diseases, but also casting out demons and healing all the various diseases that result from these unclean spirits. The power of the Holy Spirit appears in the Apostles, who had been unable to heal the epileptic from the unclean spirit at the Mount of Transfiguration (Mt 17:19), whereas now by touch or even by shadow they are able to heal all diseases and cast out demons.

5.15.1.en: The Holy Spirit who dwells in you calls you to adorn yourself with virtues and to serve those around you, so respond to His voice and do not neglect it, and then you will be a light to the world around you, and they will see the power of God and His grace in you as it was with the Apostles.

5.16.0.en: Satan stirred up the high priest and all his followers of the Sadducees who deny the Resurrection, and the teachings of the Apostles confirming the Resurrection of Christ enraged them, so they were intensely jealous for their mistaken beliefs and seized the Apostles and put them in the prison of Jerusalem. Naturally the Apostles raised their voices in prayer to God to save them and support them.

5.17.0.en: The Temple: most likely in Solomon's Porch, the most conspicuous place where the people gather, so that they might preach Christ without fear.

5.17.1.en: All the words of this life: that is, the proclamation of Christ by which we live in the world and which extends with us into eternity. An angel of the Lord came by night and opened the prison door and brought them out, then returned and shut it and asked them to go and complete the preaching. Their going out of the prison was not an escape from it, but in order to complete their ministry in the Temple, preaching eternal life.

5.17.2.en: Thus we see that the Christian's completion of his mission is more important to him than the safety of his life, because he knows that his remaining on earth is for the accomplishment of his preaching of Christ.

5.17.3.en: So take care to proclaim the truth even if you are exposed to the words and insults of those who oppose, confident of the power of God that supports you. Only seek God before you speak, that He may guide you and give you wisdom as to when and how to speak.

5.18.0.en: The Apostles entered the Temple at once in the morning, at the time when it was full of Jews who had come to say the morning prayer, and began to preach Jesus and the Resurrection, heedless of their weariness and exhaustion from keeping vigil all night in prison, because their hearts were attached to the love of God, which sustained their weak bodies. At the same time the high priest and his followers - of the Sadducees - called the members of the Sanhedrin to meet, together with all the elders of the Jews. The purpose was to punish the Apostles to prevent their preaching, so that they would thereby be rid of the preaching of Christ and this story, which troubled them, would end.

5.18.1.en: And when the council assembled they sent their servants to bring the Apostles from the prison, for they did not know that the Apostles were in the Temple.

5.19.0.en: When the servants, that is, the soldiers of the Temple, opened the prison, they found no one in it, though it had been securely locked and the guards stood before the doors.

5.19.1.en: This confirms that what happened was by the hand of an angel and not a man, and the power of God appears, which made the prison guards not feel the Apostles going out, for they were in deep sleep.

5.20.0.en: The captain of the Temple guard and the chief priests fell into perplexity and doubt, being unable to explain what had happened.

5.21.0.en: Their confusion increased when they learned that the Apostles were standing firm and had not fled, but were teaching the people in the Temple. This means their insistence on preaching in the name of Christ, rejecting the orders of the chief priests.

5.22.0.en: The captain of the Temple guard went with his soldiers and brought the Apostles without violence, fearing for their own lives, in view of the people's honor and respect for the Apostles; for if they used violence with them the Apostles would not resist them, but the people would have struck them down and stoned them.

5.23.0.en: When they stood before the council, the high priest asked them why they had disobeyed his command and continued to teach in the name of Christ. We note two things here:

5.23.1.en: He did not ask them about the miracle of their being brought out of the prison, as though it did not concern him because he refuses to believe.

5.23.2.en: He would not consent to mention the name of Christ with his tongue, so he called Him "this man," as if He were a nobody without a name, out of the excess of his hatred of Him, and his distress that the Apostles' preaching of the risen Christ exposes the error of the priests who killed Him and brings His blood upon them, forgetting what they themselves said in (Mt 27:25), "His blood be on us, and on our children."

5.24.0.en: Peter and all the Apostles declared that the commands of God, which are the words of Christ to them and what the angel commanded them, are more important than the words of men, even if they are the greatest council among the Jews, the Sanhedrin.

5.25.0.en: The Apostles said that God, the God of all the fathers in whom the Jews believe, has raised up Christ, whom they wronged and crucified.

5.26.0.en: God exalted Christ by His high divine power as Head of the Church and Savior of the whole world, calling to repentance and granting forgiveness to all believers of the Jews, since the preaching was to them first, before the Gentiles.

5.27.0.en: This is the witness of the Apostles and the witness of the Holy Spirit, who fills them as believers in Christ who obey Him.

5.27.1.en: Our observation is repeated, that witness to Christ is the center of the life of those who believe in Him in every time and place.

5.27.2.en: The Apostles seized the opportunity of their trial before the Sanhedrin to preach Christ to them, in the hope that they might repent. So do good and show love to everyone, however harsh and however much he rejects the word of God. If you show love to the beloved brother, then show manifold more to the one who wrongs you and opposes you, for he needs love more than others do, and do not despair of anyone's salvation.

5.28.0.en: As a result of the high priest's intense anger, he consulted with his followers about killing all the Apostles in order to be finished with this matter.

5.29.0.en: The Law: that is, the Torah, which is the five books of Moses.

5.29.1.en: Commanded: so that the anger of the Sadducees might subside and they might accept his words. For he was a Pharisee who believed in the Resurrection, and it seems that he was moderate and wise.

5.29.2.en: God used one of the great teachers of the Jews, Gamaliel, the son of Simeon the elder, who carried the Lord in his arms when He was presented at the Temple at the age of 40 days, and who was in turn the son of Hillel, the great Jewish teacher. Gamaliel was a man of honor and clear intellectual wisdom, and Saul of Tarsus was taught at his hands. He ordered the Apostles to be put outside for the deliberation.

5.30.0.en: Gamaliel warned those assembled against trying to kill the Apostles, because it might be unjust and therefore disobedience to God and defiance of Him.

5.31.0.en: Gamaliel gave an example of deceivers, namely "Theudas," who claimed to be a prophet or perhaps the awaited Messiah and made disciples of about 400 persons, but because he was false he perished and all his followers were scattered. So if the Apostles were deceivers like Theudas, God would destroy them and there was no need to kill them at the hands of the rulers.

5.32.0.en: Judas of Galilee: a person born in Galilee who raised a revolt against the Romans, refusing to pay them tribute, on the ground that the Jews were the people of God and paid tithes to God alone.

5.32.1.en: The taxing: this was a second census ordered by the emperor, different from the census that took place in the days of the birth of Christ, and its purpose was to register the subjects of the empire in order to collect tribute from them.

5.32.2.en: The Romans put down the revolt and killed Judas and many of his followers, and the rest fled and were scattered in many distant countries.

5.32.3.en: Gamaliel's purpose in this second example also was that the council should leave the Apostles alone, for if they were wicked, God would destroy them.

5.33.0.en: This counsel: the preaching of the Resurrection.

5.33.2.en: Gamaliel asked them to leave the Apostles to speak about the Resurrection and work miracles, being sure that if the source of this work was a man, the work would come to an end in time, but if its source was God, He would establish it and no one would be able to fight it.

5.34.0.en: They agreed with him: the work of God was powerful, so the council was moved by Gamaliel's words and was persuaded by them, although there were other viewpoints, that there was no objection to disciplining the wicked, as they supposed the Apostles to be, but the grace of God made them silent and submit to his opinion.

5.34.1.en: Thus God used Gamaliel's wisdom to save the Apostles from being killed, but the high priest vented his anger toward them by flogging them, the custom among the Romans being 39 lashes, and he renewed his charge to them to stop preaching. By the flogging he meant to frighten them so that they would turn back from preaching Christ, or to put them to shame before the people after their flogging, because flogging among the Romans is a great disgrace, and so they would also be ashamed to preach.

5.35.0.en: Contrary to what the council expected, the Apostles went out in joy and zeal for greater preaching, because they regarded the pain of the flogging as fellowship in the sufferings of Christ and a preparation for the glories of heaven.

5.36.0.en: The Apostles continued steadfast in teaching in the Temple and in the houses in the name of the Lord.

5.36.1.en: Thus they set us an example in feeling the value of the spiritual mission and being concerned to accomplish it more than a man is concerned for his personal safety. They showed us that service is not only for those who attend church, but we seek out those far away and the sick in their homes and take every opportunity to serve Christ.

5.36.2.en: They held Liturgies and Christian rites in the houses, because churches had not yet been built.

5.36.3.en: If sufferings befall you because of holding to God's commandments or serving Him, may you accept them for the sake of His love, for if Christ sacrificed His life for you, it is not much for you to endure everything for Him, but to regard these sufferings as a blessing and an honor to you, because you shared with your Savior in carrying His cross.
